Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
Compromise affidavit filed on behalf of opposite party No. 2, is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the charge sheet No. 07 of 2019 dated 14.1.2019 and cognizance order dated 29.1.2019 as well as entire criminal proceedings of S.T. No. 498 of 2019 (State vs. Mohd. Afsar and others) arising out of Case Crime No.
1044 of 2018,, under Sections 498A, 323, 307, 376, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station- Kharkhunda, District- Meerut, pending in the court of Addl. District Judge/Fast Track Court,
Meerut.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party No. 2 is the wife of applicant Mohammad Afsar And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52643746/
1 No. 1 and daughter in-law of applicant No. 2 and sister in-law of applicant No. 3 and on account of matrimonial discord, instant criminal case was instituted against the applicants, however with the intervention of the respected members of both the families, parties have amicably settled all their disputes and differences and now they do not have any grievance against each other.
Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that the parties have re-united and are living together and leading a happy married life.
Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that in view of the compromise made between the parties, the entire criminal proceedings against the applicants be quashed.
Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has also appeared and has filed an affidavit today in Court, which shall form part of this application and in paragraph-9 of the said affidavit, it has been stated that all the disputes and differences have been settled and now she does not have any grievance against each other and they have re-united and and leading a happy married life with her husband.

2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].
